evals.prompt: Add a confirmation modal before deleting a project from the dashboard.
evals.expected_output: A real, working delete flow: a delete action on each project card, a custom-styled confirmation modal (not a native browser confirm()), and a real API route performing the delete under RLS.
assertions: Does not use the native browser confirm()/alert() for the confirmation step
Confirmation modal/dialog uses shadow-based elevation (.nova-card or equivalent shadow) rather than a plain bordered box
Action buttons reuse existing shared primitives (PrimaryButton/GhostButton from src/components/ui/Button.tsx) instead of raw unstyled <button> elements
The destructive confirm action has a visible pending/loading state while the delete request is in flight
No new hardcoded hex color values are introduced outside src/lib/design-tokens.ts or globals.css

evals.prompt: The upload page feels kind of plain, make it feel more premium.
evals.expected_output: Principled visual polish grounded in the existing design tokens (shadow/elevation, type hierarchy, spacing rhythm, restrained motion) rather than surface-level changes like adding random color or a generic gradient.
assertions: Headings continue to use the Outfit/display font class and body copy the Plus Jakarta Sans/root font class, not swapped or mixed arbitrarily
No new hardcoded hex color values are introduced outside src/lib/design-tokens.ts or globals.css
Any new motion/animation is restrained (fade/lift-style) rather than bouncy or attention-grabbing easing
Elevation/depth changes use shadow-based styling (.nova-card pattern) rather than only heavier borders
Existing shared primitives (Field, PrimaryButton, StepPill, etc.) are reused rather than reimplemented inline

evals.prompt: Add a notification bell icon to the header showing recent job completions in a dropdown.
evals.expected_output: A real notification bell + dropdown component querying actual job data, with a designed empty state, reusing existing primitives/tokens, and basic keyboard/focus accessibility.
assertions: The dropdown includes a designed empty state (e.g. "no notifications yet") rather than rendering nothing or a blank list when there's no data
The dropdown/menu uses shadow-based elevation (.nova-card pattern) consistent with the rest of the app
Interactive elements (bell trigger, dropdown items) have visible focus states or aria attributes for keyboard/screen-reader accessibility
No new hardcoded hex color values are introduced outside src/lib/design-tokens.ts or globals.css
Reuses existing shared primitives/tokens rather than inventing one-off styling for the same job
